CBP employees demonstrate the highest level of commitment to protect and serve the United States of America and to exemplify the CBP Core Values of Vigilance, Service to Country and Integrity.

Learn more about CBP's mission, core values and careers at https://www.cbp.gov/about This supervisory mission support position allows you to use your knowledge and experience supervising a team that plans and carries out a wide variety of mission support, budgetary, and administrative research, and program-planning activities related to the missions and functions of the Finance Branch within the Mission Readiness Operations Division.

This position starts at a salary of $117,402.00 (GS-13, Step 1) to $152,625.00 (GS-13, Step 10). As a Supervisory Mission Support Specialist (Finance), you will perform significant review and analysis of budget, management, training, logistics, procurement, and other areas of mission support resources.

Typical work assignments will include: Supervising a team that is responsible for all aspects of the formulation, development, execution phase of the overall aspects of the organization's budget. Managing the Travel Card program by serving as the Certifier or Reviewer to fund and/or approve travel authorizations and vouchers.

Performing ongoing mentoring, training and guidance to peers, colleagues, employees and supervisors. Preparing, reviewing, and reconciling budget reports and expenditures. Forecasting and allocating organizational budgetary needs, including providing guidance, assistance, and recommendations to management.
Experience: You qualify for the GS-13 grade level if you possess 1 year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade level, performing duties such as: Performing budget analysis to analyze historical data, current spending plans, future estimates and trends.

Managing the Travel Card program to fund and/or approve travel authorizations and vouchers. Preparing special briefings and reports for management for understanding and acceptance of recommendations related to budget, procurement, and travel needs.

Managing multiple appropriations and working directly with Program Managers to secure funding for mission requirements. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is a federal law enforcement agency that requires all applicants to undergo a thorough background investigation prior to employment in order to promote the agency's core values of vigilance, service to country, and integrity.

During the screening and/or background investigation process, you will be asked questions regarding any felony criminal convictions or current felony charges, the use of illegal drugs (e.g., marijuana, cocaine, heroin, LSD, methamphetamines, ecstasy), and the use of non-prescribed controlled substances including any experimentation, possession, sale, receipt, manufacture, cultivation, production, transfer, shipping, trafficking, or distribution of controlled substances.

For additional information on the preemployment process, review the following link: Applicant Resources | CBP Careers Residency: There is a residency requirement for all applicants not currently employed by CBP.

Individuals are required to have physically resided in the United States or its protectorates (as declared under international law) for at least three of the last five years.

If you do not meet the residency requirement and you have been physically located in a foreign location for more than two of the last five years, you may request an exception to determine if you are eligible for a residency waiver by meeting one or more of the following conditions: Working for the U.S.

Government as a federal civilian or as a member of the military A dependent who was authorized to accompany a federal civilian or member of the military who was working for the U.S. government Participation in a study abroad program sponsored by a U.S. affiliated college or university Working as a contractor, intern, consultant or volunteer supporting the U.S. government Probationary Period: All employees new to the federal government must serve a one year probationary period during the first year of his/her initial permanent federal appointment to determine fitness for continued employment.

Current and former federal employees may be required to serve or complete a probationary period.

Deine Mission
Mach die Energiewende erlebbar – mit exzellentem Kundenservice!

Kundenanfragen bearbeiten: Du beantwortest Anfragen per E-Mail und Telefon, löst Probleme und sorgst für eine positive Customer Experience.
Prozesse optimieren: Du erkennst Verbesserungspotenziale in den Abläufen und bringst Vorschläge zur Optimierung ein.
Teamaufbau unterstützen: Du hilfst dabei, Strukturen zu schaffen und neue Teammitglieder einzuarbeiten.
Feedback weitergeben: Du sammelst Kund:innen-Insights und arbeitest eng mit Produkt und Operations zusammen, um unsere Services zu verbessern.

Du liebst es, Kund:innen zu helfen, und findest für jedes Problem eine Lösung.
Du arbeitest strukturiert, eigenverantwortlich und effizient.
Du hast bereits erste Erfahrungen im Customer Service.
Du bist kommunikationsstark – auf Deutsch und idealerweise auch auf Englisch.

Wir freuen uns auf Deinen Einsatz in unserem Office in Köln oder Berlin. Grundsätzlich kannst du hybrid von überall aus arbeiten, uns ist aber ein naher Bezug zu unserem Team und damit regelmäßige Teamtreffen vor Ort wichtig.

From Fivetran’s founding until now, our mission has remained the same: to make access to data as simple and reliable as electricity. Starforge Systems is looking for a Technical Customer Support Representative to remotely troubleshoot Windows-based gaming PCs and help customers resolve hardware, software, and performance issues.
This is not a general help-desk or password-reset position. You will regularly investigate problems involving system instability, blue screens, driver conflicts, failed components, performance issues, Windows errors, and PCs that do not boot or display properly. You will own each case through its full lifecycle, from initial diagnosis through resolution, repair, or escalation to another internal team.
Most customer communication is handled through email. Because you will not have the computer in front of you, you must be able to gather useful information, interpret diagnostic results, and guide customers of varying technical skill levels through troubleshooting safely and clearly.
Scheduled troubleshooting calls are also available to customers. New representatives will not begin taking calls immediately, but prior experience providing technical support by phone with or without screen share is a strong advantage.

Investigate and resolve customer-reported hardware, software, stability, and performance issues affecting Windows PCs
Communicate with customers primarily through email, with scheduled troubleshooting calls added after training and onboarding
Ask targeted questions that distinguish between hardware failures, software conflicts, configuration problems, and user-environment issues
Review and interpret diagnostic information such as crash dumps, Windows Event Viewer entries, reliability history, temperatures, hardware-monitoring data, and stress-test results
Guide customers through remote troubleshooting, including driver installation or removal, BIOS changes, Windows repair procedures, hardware reseating, component testing, and operating-system reinstallation
Troubleshoot common issues involving graphics cards, memory, storage drives, processors, motherboards, cooling, power delivery, networking, peripherals, and Windows
Determine when additional troubleshooting is appropriate and when a component replacement, repair, or full-system return is the correct next step
Document symptoms, troubleshooting performed, test results, and conclusions thoroughly within the ticketing system
Escalate urgent, unusual, safety-related, or unresolved issues with a clear summary of the situation and work already completed
Collaborate with other support representatives, repair technicians, quality-control staff, and operations teams to resolve customer issues
Stay current on supported hardware, Windows updates, driver releases, known product issues, and internal support procedures

Demonstrated hands-on experience building, repairing, or troubleshooting Windows desktop PCs
Practical understanding of desktop computer components and how failures in one component may present as symptoms elsewhere in the system
Experience diagnosing Windows crashes, freezes, boot failures, driver problems, hardware instability, and performance issues
Ability to independently interpret diagnostic results and explain the reasoning behind a recommended next step
Familiarity with Windows tools and procedures such as, Event Viewer, Device Manager, Windows crash dumps or bug-check information, System File Checker and DISM, Safe Mode and Windows Recovery Environment. Driver installation and clean removal, Disk Management, Windows installation, and reset procedures
Familiarity with PC diagnostic and testing utilities such as DDU, MemTest86, HWiNFO or HWMonitor, and hardware stress-testing software

Strong written communication skills, including the ability to provide complete instructions without overwhelming or talking down to the customer

​ The Floating Medical Office Customer Service position provides temporary administrative coverage to different medical practices when staffing gaps occur due to vacations, sick leave, resignations, increased workload, or other unexpected absences.

Unlike an assistant dedicated to a single client, the floating assistant must be able to quickly adapt to different providers, workflows, software systems, and operational protocols while maintaining service quality and minimizing disruption to the client.

The position follows a rapid deployment model, meaning the floating assistant is not permanently assigned to a fixed group of clients. Instead, onboarding is provided when coverage is required for a specific medical practice.
Responsibilities Responsibilities will depend on the workflows and operational requirements of each assigned medical practice and may include:
Following appointment scheduling rules and provider preferences.
Supporting insurance workflows.
Assisting with referral processes.
Supporting prior authorization procedures.
Following patient communication protocols and telephone scripts.
Following established escalation procedures.
Maintaining internal documentation standards.
Navigating Electronic Medical Record (EMR) systems.
Reviewing and following client-specific documentation and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
Following daily operational processes and checklists.
Adapting to different medical practices, workflows, software systems, and operational protocols.

s.h: Must have your own device and headset
s.t:
High-speed internet connection of at least 100 MB.
Previous experience working with U.S.-based medical offices and knowledge of HIPAA regulations.
Ability to quickly adapt to different medical practices, providers, workflows, and operational protocols.
Ability to continuously learn and transition between different client environments.
Ability to learn and navigate different Electronic Medical Record (EMR) systems and software platforms.
Ability to understand and follow practice-specific scheduling rules, insurance workflows, referral processes, prior authorization procedures, and patient communication protocols.
Ability to follow telephone scripts, escalation procedures, and internal documentation standards.
Ability to review and follow Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), operational guides, and daily checklists.
Ability to work effectively following an accelerated onboarding process for each new assignment.

s.h: Previous experience with medical offices is preferred.
s.t:
Systems Medical practices may use different software platforms, including:
Athenahealth
eClinicalWorks
Nextech
HealthArc
EMA
Other proprietary systems
The position requires the ability to understand not only the software used by each practice, but also the operational processes and procedures established by that particular medical office.

s.h: Assignment and Onboarding Model When coverage is required
s.t:
A client reports an upcoming absence or unexpected staffing need.
A floating assistant is assigned.
The assistant receives an accelerated onboarding.
The assistant reviews the client's documentation.
The assistant begins providing temporary coverage until the assigned employee returns.
Because medical offices may operate differently, each assignment may require adaptation to new workflows, provider preferences, software systems, and operational procedures. Comprehensive client documentation, structured onboarding, and ongoing support during the initial stages of each assignment are key components of the floating coverage model.

As a Front Line Manager you will: Plan work to be accomplished by subordinates, sets and adjusts short-term priorities and prepares schedules for completion of work. Assign work to subordinates based on priorities, selective consideration of the difficulty and requirements of assignments, and the capabilities of employees.

Evaluate work performance of subordinates and makes recommendations for outstanding performance recognition and/or disciplinary action. Give advice, counsel or instruction to employees on work and administrative matters.

Interview candidates for positions within the organization/unit and recommend appointment, promotion or reassignment to such positions. Hear and resolve complaints from employees, refer group grievances and/or more serious unresolved complaints as appropriate.

Effect minor disciplinary measures, such as warnings and reprimands, recommend other actions in more serious cases. Identify developmental and training needs of employees, providing or arranging for needed development and training. Initiate ways to improve production, work processes and/or to increase the quality of the work directed.

The following are the job specific duties of this position. You will have the opportunity to learn to perform these duties and receive training to help you grow in this position. Provides leadership and direction to employees performing technical work involving taxpayer inquiries, case analysis, and resolution of complex tax issues.

Plans, organizes, and assigns work based on program priorities, workload complexity, and employee capabilities to ensure timely and accurate completion of assignments.

Monitors work in progress and reviews completed work for quality, accuracy, and adherence to applicable tax laws, regulations, and Internal Revenue Manual (IRM) procedures, taking corrective action as needed.

Ensures timely and accurate resolution of inventory and monitors aged inventory using available reports and systems to prevent overage conditions. Provides technical oversight of taxpayer inquiries and case resolution activities by evaluating work performed and ensuring consistent application of tax laws, regulations, and IRM procedures.

Reviews and analyzes cases involving multiple issue areas, complex regulatory requirements, and frequently changing guidance to ensure accurate and compliant resolution. Ensures employees follow established procedures for handling inventory, system usage, and case documentation requirements.

Analyzes workload, production data, and program trends to assess performance, identify risks, and recommend improvements. Uses automated systems and reports to monitor inventory, evaluate productivity, and support data-driven decisions.

Obtains and analyzes quality review data (e.g., Embedded Quality, National Quality, and other review systems) to identify errors, trends, and opportunities for improvement, and provides feedback to employees. Manages administrative functions, including leave, time and attendance, and staffing, and resolves employee concerns at the appropriate level.

Performs conduct and leave counseling, and promotes a work environment that supports employee engagement, motivation, and retention. Applies advanced interviewing and analytical techniques to evaluate taxpayer circumstances, including sensitive financial and personal information, and to determine appropriate actions.

Ensures proper handling of cases involving issues such as compliance determinations, financial hardship, or potential noncompliance. Evaluates determinations made by employees to ensure sound judgment in resolving discrepancies and interpreting taxpayer intent.

Ensures proper handling of sensitive taxpayer data and reinforces adherence to disclosure and privacy regulations in all case interactions. Coordinates workflow to ensure efficient case resolution and compliance activities.

Determines staffing needs and develops schedules to ensure adequate coverage and alignment with program requirements, including adherence to workload demands and operational priorities. Advises management on operational issues, risks, and improvement opportunities, and ensures compliance with policies, procedures, and quality standards.
